title: The last week, looking back
hook: a donkey, a towel, a garden, a cross, a garden again
carry: the week that turned the world
tomorrow: how did a story from one garden reach your street?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Mary: a yes first, and a heart that kept what it couldn't yet explain. Keep it in your heart. Today, the week she watched from close by.
screen: `KEEP IT IN YOUR HEART.` → `THE WEEK SHE WATCHED.`

segments.voice: A junk drawer can hold a whole year: a ticket stub, a hospital bracelet, the key to an old apartment. The Gospels' last week fits in five objects. A donkey. A towel. A garden. A cross. And a garden again. Christians call it Holy Week. It starts with a cheering crowd and ends in a quiet garden, early in the morning. Laid side by side, the five show what one very hard week can hold.
screen: `A YEAR IN A JUNK DRAWER.` → `A DONKEY, A TOWEL, A GARDEN.` → `A CROSS, A GARDEN AGAIN.`

segments.voice: The donkey first. Jesus rides into Jerusalem, and Mark says “they brought the colt to Jesus, and cast their garments on him; and he sat upon him.” A king, arriving on a borrowed colt. Then the towel. At supper, John says, Jesus “riseth from supper, and laid aside his garments; and took a towel, and girded himself,” and washes his friends' feet. Peter protests. Jesus kneels anyway, and afterward says, “ye also ought to wash one another's feet.” Then a garden at night, Gethsemane, where he prays in anguish and ends, “nevertheless not what I will, but what thou wilt.” Then the cross. Roman soldiers crucify him under Pilate, and Luke records him praying, “Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do.” And the garden again. John notices it: “in the place where he was crucified there was a garden; and in the garden a new sepulchre.” Early on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene is weeping there and takes the risen Jesus for the gardener, until he says her name. Here's the thing to tell a friend: of the five objects, the towel is the one Jesus tells his friends to pick up. In a hard week of an ordinary life, not much gets said out loud. Someone can still kneel and serve, pray honestly, forgive, and call another person by name.
screen: `THE COLT INTO JERUSALEM.` · `A TOWEL, AND WASH ONE ANOTHER'S FEET.` · `GETHSEMANE, THEN THE CROSS.` · `A NAME IN THE GARDEN.` · then, large: `THE WEEK THAT TURNED THE WORLD.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and walk the week one object at a time: the donkey, the towel, the garden, the cross, the garden again. Stay longest wherever you find yourself stopping. If you pray, pray there; if not, just stay with what you see.
The last week. The days from Jesus's ride into Jerusalem to the empty tomb, which Christians call Holy Week.
The line to keep: the week that turned the world, with a towel in the middle of it. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Churches that keep Holy Week mark it with Palm Sunday, a supper or foot-washing on Thursday, Good Friday services and an Easter vigil or sunrise service, each tradition in its own way.

fork.setup: a coworker's dad died this week, and you don't know what to say at the funeral. which object from the last week fits best?
options: the towel: say little, and do one humble, useful thing.
the donkey: arrive in a big way so everyone knows you came.
the cross: explain to them that suffering always has a reason.
fork.reveal: at the supper Jesus said little, knelt with a towel, and told his friends, ye also ought to wash one another's feet.

trapdoor: what you thought: the last week is only the story of how Jesus died.
what it means: a week of humility, service, surrender and forgiveness that ends with a name in a garden.
what a scholar hears: John notes a garden at the place of the crucifixion, with a new sepulchre in it (John 19:41).
guess: Jesus's final days, from Jerusalem to the empty tomb
the final week of a year of Bible lessons
the week before Christmas in the church year

chat.says: dad still hasn't said a word about chicago. but i found my car washed this morning. inside AND out.
options: That might be his towel. Some people say it by serving. Thank him for the car.
He's avoiding it. Washing a car is just stress; wait for actual words.
Sweet, but it's not an answer. Love only counts once it's said out loud.
chat.meaning: At the supper Jesus knelt with a towel instead of a speech, and asked his friends to do the same. Love that week came as service.

Gethsemane.meaning: a garden outside Jerusalem where Jesus prayed at night

Pilate.meaning: the Roman governor who sentenced Jesus

Mary Magdalene.meaning: a follower of Jesus, first to meet him risen in John

Holy Week.meaning: the week before Easter, from Palm Sunday on

Grace: her dad Marcus still hasn't talked about Chicago, but washes her car without a word.
Crucifixion framed as carried out by Roman soldiers under Pilate (Mark 15), per the guide. One gentle line only; no graphic detail.
'A borrowed colt' paraphrases Mark 11:2–6 (the colt is untied and the owners let it go when told 'the Lord hath need of him'). Confirm.

'Of the five objects, the towel is the one Jesus tells his friends to pick up' rests on John 13:14–15. Confirm the framing (the supper's bread and cup are also commanded in other Gospels; the line speaks only of the five objects in the index).
Original game: Greek lention (towel), John 13:4. Confirm accents and sound-out.
